common_fields.event_id: UNASSIGNED (JSON null): installation-immutable identity assigned by the M1 transaction, never an engine field or content hash.
common_fields.ingestion_seq: UNASSIGNED (JSON null): installation commit order assigned by the M1 transaction with its checkpoint.
common_fields.schema_version: Adapter constant 1; input schema_version is ignored.
common_fields.sensor_id: Verified local Context.SensorID; input sensor_id is ignored.
common_fields.engine: Adapter constant cowrie or web; input engine is ignored.
common_fields.observed_at: Engine timestamp parsed as RFC3339Nano and normalized to UTC. Missing/invalid timestamps stay null and are flagged. More than 5 minutes after the optional local ReferenceTime is flagged.
common_fields.ingested_at: UNASSIGNED (JSON null): DB collection time assigned by M1. Neither engine timestamp nor local ReferenceTime stands in for a committed collection time.
common_fields.source_ip: Socket-observed src_ip (Cowrie) or peer_ip (web), parsed by net/netip and Unmap. Headers, body, query, input source_ip and forwarded claims cannot set this field.
common_fields.source_port: Socket-observed src_port (Cowrie) or peer_port (web); 1..65535. Missing remains 0 with source_missing, never replaced with a client local port or forwarded value.
common_fields.destination_ip: Context.PublicIP only after exact normalized observed destination IP AND port match Context.ObservedIP/ObservedPort for this sensor and service. Raw container address is never published as destination.
common_fields.destination_port: Context.PublicPort only after the same verified endpoint match. A missing raw endpoint leaves public destination unassigned with destination_missing; mismatch is rejected.
common_fields.service: Verified local Context.Service (ssh/http/https). Cowrie requires ssh; web protocol must match the configured service.
common_fields.event_type: Allowlisted Cowrie eventid TYPE, or exact web event_type=web.request. Cowrie eventid is not a unique engine event identity.
common_fields.session_id: Cowrie session supplied by engine, bounded structural identifier; absent session is flagged. Web has no session identifier in this envelope.
common_fields.attributes: Typed allowlist of redacted credentials/command or method/URI/headers/body/parser metadata. Nullable unavailable fields are omitted, observed empty strings/arrays retained; field_completeness records web availability. Freeform messages and unknown fields/reasons are omitted.
common_fields.source_cursor: Trusted local Context.Cursor: file_generation_id plus byte_offset at record start. Neither supported engine provides a stable unique event ID. Equal bytes at different positions remain distinct observations.
common_fields.raw_hash: SHA-256 of exact supplied incoming record bytes BEFORE redaction/normalization. Fixture tests supply each JSONL line excluding LF; offsets include LF. Caller-supplied LF/whitespace is hashed if included. This detects byte changes, does not attest truth, and must never be a deduplication key.
common_fields.quality_flags: Fixed adapter enums plus allowlisted engine quality/parser flags; unknown strings become generic flags without copying text. Truncation, unavailable fields, parse limits, metadata contradictions, time anomalies, redaction limits and trusted collection gaps remain visible.
common_fields.is_test: Trusted local Context.IsTest only. Raw is_test/auto_report_eligible, HTTP headers/query/body and Cowrie input cannot assign test provenance.

engines.hash_scope: fixture_sha256 hashes the committed sanitized JSONL including LF; original_raw_sha256 hashes private original engine bytes, a distinct provenance fact. Row raw_hash hashes only the committed fixture record supplied to this adapter.

field_mapping.dst_ip/dst_port: exact observed-endpoint match against Context, then destination_ip/destination_port from Context public mapping
field_mapping.engine stable event ID: unavailable; use local file generation and byte offset

engines.original_per_record_hashes: Not present in existing expected.json; do not invent from sanitized fixture bytes.

engines.hash_scope: fixture_sha256 hashes the committed sanitized JSONL including LF; original_raw_sha256 hashes private original engine bytes, a distinct provenance fact. Row raw_hash hashes only the committed fixture record supplied to this adapter.

field_mapping.destination_ip/destination_port: exact observed-endpoint match against Context, then public destination mapping
field_mapping.method/uri/headers/body: bounded redacted attributes; null stays unavailable
field_mapping.parse_error: allowlisted attributes.parse_error and quality; unknown text omitted
field_mapping.field_completeness: derived safe field availability, metadata absence/contradiction flagged; arbitrary source/reason text omitted
field_mapping.truncation: original engine counts preserved separately from adapter clipping flags
field_mapping.quality_flags: fixed allowlist; unknown flags replaced by engine_quality_unknown
field_mapping.auto_report_eligible/is_test: ignored; test provenance only from Context.IsTest
field_mapping.wire_sha256/wire_bytes: omitted from canonical attributes; these describe received wire bytes, not raw_hash of the record
field_mapping.engine stable event ID/session ID: unavailable; use local file generation and byte offset

limit_policy.record: Reject input over 262144 bytes, invalid UTF-8, malformed/nonobject/trailing JSON, duplicate or case-colliding object keys, or nesting deeper than 64 with fixed payload-free errors.
limit_policy.uri: At most 8192 bytes. Oversize or ambiguous percent/query parsing is withheld, with uri_truncated and/or uri_redaction_limited flags; secret query values and URL userinfo are removed.
limit_policy.headers: At most 16384 original bytes total, counting name + value + 4 framing bytes per header; retain whole headers only. Known authentication/cookie/token values are redacted. Forwarded headers may remain attributes but never influence source. Redacted output header bytes are independently capped at the same limit because markers can increase short values.
limit_policy.body: At most 16384 bytes. JSON and form bodies are structurally redacted; truncated structured bodies, malformed/duplicate JSON, ambiguous encodings, unsupported media types and content codings are withheld with body_redaction_limited. Safe plain text and nonsecret structured values remain evidence. Non-UTF-8/non-ASCII declared charset, content-transfer-encoding and structured data labeled plain text are also withheld.
limit_policy.command: At most 16384 bytes. Known credential labels/options (including attached -pVALUE and -uUSER:VALUE) and encoding ambiguity withhold the command with quality flags. Any single quote, double quote or backslash withholds the whole command with command_redacted and command_redaction_limited because the adapter does not interpret shell quoting or escapes. Ordinary unambiguous nonsecret commands remain evidence. This is not universal shell credential detection.
limit_policy.engine_truncation: attributes.truncation preserves valid original engine limit/observed/retained/truncated values. Retained counts precede engine/fixture redaction and need not equal the length of redacted strings. Adapter clipping is indicated separately by adapter_uri_limit, adapter_headers_limit or adapter_body_limit; no original byte count is overwritten.

trust_boundary: These functions consume envelopes written by the verified engine, not arbitrary network JSON as authoritative transport metadata. The engine remains the source of socket observations; raw_hash does not make a dishonest engine trustworthy. There is no network I/O, code execution, DB, API, report dispatch or River integration.
missing_information: Installation event identity, commit ordering, DB collection time and atomic checkpoint assignment remain M1 responsibilities.
Both envelopes lack a stable unique engine event ID; collector must establish file generations and start offsets, including rotation/truncation handling in M1.
Redacted or withheld evidence cannot reconstruct the original secret. Structured ambiguity is explicitly limited, not represented as complete evidence.
Public destination mappings are verified local settings; no public destination is inferred from internal addresses, request Host headers or attacker claims.
ReferenceTime is optional local clock evidence; absent reference is flagged time_reference_unavailable. Missing/invalid observed time is never replaced by collection time.
Cowrie fixtures were sanitized before this adapter and omit freeform messages, client version details and other fields outside the exporter allowlist.
Web malformed/limited cases contain unavailable fields, and body/URI/header truncation remains incomplete. An event is not automatically report-eligible merely because it decodes.
Supported runtime validation remains Linux ARM64 and public IPv4. IPv6 and IPv4-mapped IPv6 normalization are unit-level evidence only; public IPv6 is NOT_SUPPORTED.
These offline adapters do not validate M0-06 overall GO, durability, report rules, authenticity, arbitrary future engine event schemas or unknown credential formats.
